commands.seed: for r in "Widget:3:1250" "Gasket:12:499" "Flange:1:19999"; do IFS=: read -r n q p <<< "$r"; curl -fsS -o /dev/null -X POST --data-urlencode "name=$n" --data-urlencode "qty=$q" --data-urlencode "price=$p" "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT:-3000}/add"; done

env.name: PORT
env.why: The only variable this app reads. src/server.js:15 is `var port = process.env.PORT || 3000`, and that port is the whole of the app's own origin: there is no base-URL setting, no allowlist and no callback URL anywhere in src/. 3000 is set explicitly rather than left to the default so that app_url and the runbook cannot drift from what the process actually binds. The test suites now open do not depend on it: every one of them binds an ephemeral port through the `module.exports = app` seam in src/server.js rather than reusing PORT, so the tests gate and a running app cannot collide on 3000.

dropped.why: Linting is the static gate's job: `bsf gates static` runs the repo's own linter and compares each rule's per-file count against .factory/guardrails/baselines.json. Putting it in `build` or `test` would make a baselined lint violation fail the trial as a build error and would count the same finding twice. It is still runnable in the sandbox — `npm run lint` works once `npm ci` has run — it is just not in the build path.

Replaced with `npm ci`, which installs exactly what the committed package-lock.json pins and fails loudly if the lock file and package.json disagree, so the sandbox cannot silently resolve a different dependency tree from one round to the next. `npm ci` was the command actually run and verified here; `npm install` was not.

Replaced with the equivalent `node src/server.js`. The trial stops the app by signalling the detached process group, and running node directly means there is no npm wrapper process between the signal and the server. `npm start` is kept in the runbook as the command a developer would type; the two run the same file.

dropped.what: `npm test` exactly as the report worded it
dropped.why: Set to `npm test --if-present` instead, which is the same command wherever a `test` script exists and differs only where none does. The report's own pull request (#12) is open, not merged, so the default branch still has no `test` script, and factory-setup-trial.yml checks out the branch the workflow runs on. Measured here on the default branch after `npm ci`: bare `npm test` exits 1 with `npm error Missing script: "test"`, and `reachedTier` in the runner returns `static` the moment the test step fails, skipping the run and screenshot steps entirely. Taking the report's wording literally would therefore have measured `static` and frozen a worse sandbox than the one already in place, without running anyone's tests. There is no third option: a command that passes on a tree with no test script cannot also fail on one, so `--if-present` is the only wording that is both correct on the default branch today and correct on every pull request that adds a suite.

dropped.what: naming the test runner directly, e.g. `node --test` or `node --test --experimental-test-coverage ...`
dropped.why: Five pull requests that add a first test suite are open at once and they do not agree: #11 and #15 use plain `node --test`, #12 adds a `pretest` hook that creates coverage/, #13 and #14 inline `mkdir -p coverage &&` before the runner; two put tests in test/ and three in tests/; #11 and #15 emit no coverage report at all. The one thing all five share is that `npm test` is how they are run. Driving the suite through npm rather than naming a runner means this manifest does not pick a winner among them and does not need another amendment when a different one merges.

`npm ci` from the committed package-lock.json: 159 packages, exit 0. Round 1 ran it under `env -i` with only PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, CI and PORT and it passed; this amendment could not repeat that control, because `env -i` also drops the proxy variables this runner's firewall needs and the install then fails to resolve the registry. The plain `npm ci` was re-run and passed.
`npm run lint` with the repo's own eslint.config.mjs, which the static gate drives.

The repo's own test suite, through `npm test --if-present`. Measured against the head of pull request #12, the tree the amendment report came from: after `npm ci`, 31 tests, 0 failures, exit 0, in about 0.3s. The suite adds no dependency — it is node's built-in runner with node:test and node:assert, and it drives the real express app through the `module.exports = app` seam in src/server.js on an ephemeral port. This is the command `bsf gates tests` runs verbatim through bash in the repo root against a pull request's own head commit, where the `test` script exists.

That the coverage gate can read what that suite writes. `npm test --if-present` on #12's tree produces coverage/lcov.info with one `SF:` record per file under src/, paths already relative (`SF:src/db.js`), which is exactly what `readCoverage` in the runner looks for first after coverage/coverage-summary.json. Reported total 98.04% line coverage: 100% of db.js, handlers.js, report.js and util.js, 82.61% of server.js with lines 18–21 (the `require.main` listen guard) uncovered. factory-gates.yml runs `bsf gates tests` before `bsf gates coverage` in the same job, so the report is on disk by the time the coverage gate reads it.

That a red test actually reaches the gate rather than being swallowed: a deliberately failing assertion appended to #12's tests/util.test.js made `npm test --if-present` exit 1; restoring the file returned it to exit 0.

That the command depends on this repo and not on the machine, which is what the trial's empty-directory control step measures: in a directory with no package.json, `npm test --if-present` exits 254 — as does bare `npm test` — so the control step still shows the command testing this repo's code.

That the command is safe on the default branch as it stands today, before any suite has merged: `npm test --if-present` after `npm ci` exits 0 having run nothing, so the trial's install → test → control → run sequence still reaches the app and measures renders.

not_exercised.what: Total coverage, until a test suite merges
not_exercised.why: commands.test is now `npm test --if-present`, so the tests gate has a command to run and is no longer blind — but what it runs depends on the branch it runs on. On the default branch today there is still no `test` script and no test file: five pull requests that add one are open at once (#11, #12, #13, #14, #15) and none has merged. There the command exits 0 having run nothing, no coverage report is written, and total coverage stays at the 0% floor in .factory/guardrails/coverage.json, so diff coverage (diff_min_pct: 80) is what has teeth. On a pull request that carries a suite the gate gets the real run, which is what the report asked for. Two consequences worth stating plainly. First, on a branch with no `test` script the tests gate now reports success rather than the neutral it reported when commands.test was null; that is a weaker signal, and it is the price of the trial being able to measure the manifest at all while the suite is unmerged. Second, whether total coverage can ever be measured depends on which pull request lands: #12, #13 and #14 emit coverage/lcov.info and #11 and #15 emit nothing. Once a `test` script is on the default branch, a further amendment should drop `--if-present`, so that deleting the script fails the gate instead of passing it quietly.

not_exercised.what: Anything that has to survive a restart
not_exercised.why: The store is two module-level variables in src/db.js (`items` and `nextId`). Every restart empties the table and resets ids to 1, and nothing is written to disk. A change about durability, a schema, a migration or a move to a real database cannot be verified here; it would need a database service added by an amendment episode.

One node process holding state in its own heap: no cluster mode, no worker pool, no lock and no transaction. Two requests interleaving inside db.add or db.remove cannot be reproduced, and nothing about state shared across processes can be checked. The test suites now open work around the same fact rather than escaping it: src/db.js exposes no reset, so they empty the store through db.remove between tests and may not hardcode an id.

not_exercised.what: HTTPS, a reverse proxy, a non-localhost origin, or any deployment concern
not_exercised.why: The app listens on plain HTTP and the sandbox reaches it at 127.0.0.1:3000. The repo has no Dockerfile, compose file, devcontainer or deploy configuration, so there is nothing here that describes another origin. Secure cookie flags, `trust proxy`, CORS, HSTS and host-based routing have no environment in this sandbox to be checked against.

express is the single runtime dependency and src/ makes no outbound network call of any kind, so there is nothing to stub and no provider test mode to name. The stubs list is empty because none is needed, not because one was skipped. A change that adds an outbound call needs an amendment episode to add its stub before it can be verified.
